newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungarian shares extend losses, pull BUX lower.
newsitem.headline: Hungarian shares extend losses, pull BUX lower.

text.p: Hungarian share prices extended Tuesday's losses on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday and ended lower for the second successive session, traders said.
The BUX index closed at 3,585.77 points, down 46.47.
Traders said today's fall did not surprise the market.
"There was a slight correction. The market already expected it," said Gabor Borda of Concorde Securities.
Chemical company Borsodchem closed a little weaker but dealers said its price movements reflected quite a good performance considering that a private placement in its shares is underway.
"Borsodchem's price is holding quite well despite the fact that its private placement is in progress," Borda said.
Borsodchem closed at 2,960 forints, down 40 and also below the daily peak of 2,990.
Hungarian privatisation agency APV Rt is currently offering 1.2 million shares and Global Depositary Receipts (GDRs) in Borsodchem to domestic and foreign institutional investors.
Some other chemical and energy shares were rangetraded and closed little changed.
Chemical firms TVK slipped five forints to end at 1,360 forints. Oil company MOL lost five forints to end at 1,600.
But gas company Primagaz bucked the trend and rose to a new high of 6,650 forint before closing at 6,640, up 90. However, its turnover was thin.
The corporate side is mostly calm but the central bank's most recent preliminary macroeconomic figures may give a boost to the bourse, Revesz said.
The main reason for Revesz's optimism was the central bank's inflation forecast for 1996 which saw a 20 percent year-on-year inflation.
"Hopefully the corrective phase will bottom out tomorrow and the bourse will resume a rising path," Tamas Revesz of Gog Securities said.
BUX index futures ended mixed, closing higher for the three forthcoming maturities by between 2.50 to 9.00 points, weakening for two and remaining steady for the longest termin.
